page: Microsoft Azure E20_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine managed under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Supporting two threads per core, the CPU subsystem features 48 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 160 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU capacity. Neither bundled local storage nor discrete GPUs are provided with this instance profile.

Benchmark measurements place overall compute and memory metrics within expected mid-tier ranges. The CPU registers a stress-ng multi-core performance value of 19418.56 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11025.0. In memory throughput testing, the platform records uncached large-block read speeds of 112.06 GB/sec and write speeds of 59.15 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks demonstrate 19.7 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside a PassMark database score of 9953.34. While small 135M parameter language model text generation reaches a strong 273.66 tokens per second, inference throughput falls sharply on larger 70B parameter models.

The primary tradeoff of the E20_v5 lies in its disaggregated storage profile. By omitting local NVMe drives, the instance limits hypervisor-level disk management overhead, presenting cost-effective memory density for architectures backed by network block storage. This resource balance fits memory-intensive applications requiring substantial RAM relative to core counts, such as Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise relational databases, medium-scale data science pipelines, and memory-heavy ETL processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E20_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. The instance provides 20 vCPUs across 10 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 160 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. It features an advanced instruction set including AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic acceleration, while lacking bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place its single-core and multi-core processing speeds within middle-tier expectations, yielding 19.7 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and solid throughput in small-scale language model generation. With uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 112 GB/sec, this instance provides cost-efficient memory density for scale-up relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, and data analytics pipelines that utilize remote network storage.
